texts.preamble: This Writ Petition Is Filed To Declare ... vs Unknown on 5 September, 2023 Author: K. Sreenivasa Reddy Bench: K. Sreenivasa Reddy Hon'Ble Sri Justice K. Sreenivasa Reddy Writ Petition No.20730 of 2023
texts.facts: Order: This Writ Petition is filed to declare the action of the respondents herein in opening and continuing the suspect sheet No.474, dated 15.11.2019, against the petitioner herein, as illegal and arbitrary. 2. Case of the Writ Petitioner, in brief, is that in the year 2018 a case in Crime No.132 of 2018 of Nellore IV Town Police Station, Dargamitta, SPSR Nellore district was registered against him for the offences punishable under Sections 353, 272, 273 read with 34 IPC and Section 59(i) of the Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006, alleging that he was transporting prohibited tobacco products. Aggrieved by the same, he filed quash petition in Crl.P.No.2557 of 2023 and this Court, by an order dated 11.04.2023, allowed the said Criminal Petition and [LEAKAGE_MASK] the proceedings in the above said crime against the petitioner herein. The further case of the petitioner herein is that except the above said crime, no other crime was registered against him and in spite of that the respondent police opened rowdy sheet against him. Hence, he filed the present Writ Petition. A counter affidavit has been filed on behalf of respondent No.4 stating that the petitioner herein is involved in Crime No.132 of 2018 of Nellore IV Town Police Station, Dargamitta, SPSR Nellore district, registered for the offences punishable under Sections 353, 272, 273 read with 34 IPC and Section 59(i) of the Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006 and the same is under investigation. It is further stated that to curb and curtail the unlawful activities of the petitioner herein in the vicinity, the SHO, IV Town Police Station, Dargamitta, Nellore of SPSR Nellore district, opened suspect sheet against the petitioner herein after getting permission from the Sub-Divisional Police Officer, Nellore Town, vide C.No.27/GL-SDPON(T)/2019, dated 15.11.2019, and subsequently the said suspect sheet was transferred to Nellore Rural Police Station on 15.03.2021, since the petitioner is residing at Nellore Rural Police Station limits.
texts.arguments: It is further stated that as per APPM Order No.601, the following persons may be classified as rowdies and rowdy sheets may be opened for them under the orders of the SP/DCP and ACP/SDPO. "1. Persons, who habitually commit, attempt to commit or abet the commission of offences involving a breach of the peace, disturbances to public order and security. 2. Persons bound over under Sections 106, 107, 108(1) and 110(e) and (g) of Cr.P.C. 3. Persons who have been convicted more than once in two consecutive years under Sections 59 and 70 SRK, J 3 WP No.20730 of 2023 of the Hyderabad City police Act or under Section 3, Clause 12 of the AP Town Nuisances Act. 4. Persons who habitually tease women and girls and pass indecent remarks including offences under This Writ Petition Is Filed To Declare ... vs Unknown on 5 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158062656/ 2 Sections 354-A, B, C and 354-D IPC. 5. Persons who have been charge sheeted under the offence of Rape (376, 376-A, B, C, D and E IPC). 6. Persons who have been charge sheeted under the offences of POCSO Act, 2012 and Acid Attacks (326A and 326B of IPC). 7. 8. Persons who intimidate by threats or use of physical violence or other unlawful means to part with movable or immovable properties or in the habit of collecting money by extortion from shopkeepers, traders and other residents including loan sharks. 9. Persons who incite, instigate and participate in communal/caste or political riots. Clause 1 of Police Standing Order No.601 contemplates that rowdy sheets may be opened against the persons, who habitually commit, attempt to commit or abet the commission of offences involving a breach of the peace, disturbances to public order and security.
